messages:
emma: Heads-up: BlueFin has verbally committed to a monthly reserved pool. They want our proposal for sizing, preheat strategy, and security answers (HSM + KMS). Peak profile: 320 QPS chat, 45 QPS embeddings; 90% short prompts (~30 tokens in, 70 out). Can we put together a concrete recommendation + POC plan?
nate: Nice. Do we know burst pattern? sustained vs spiky?
emma: Sales says traffic is bursty during payroll runs: two 45-min peaks per day, plus occasional ad-hoc spikes. Average daily traffic low outside peaks.
vijay: Quick token math: 320*(30+70)=320*100=32k tokens/s during peak -> about 2.8B tokens if that was constant. But since it's concentrated, reserved baseline can be much smaller.
maria: Proposal idea: reserve for 50% of peak (so ~160 QPS capacity) and rely on burst credits + prewarmed burst nodes for the rest. Fleet suggestion: 3x A30-equivalent for baseline, 1x A100-80GB prewarmed for burst hot path, plus 2x smaller T4-like nodes for embeddings. This mixes cost and memory.
emma: Also suggest an int8-quantized variant for cost fallback; performance note: int8 gives ~1.25x throughput on our stack with small quality delta.
arjun: On autoscale policy: recommend aggressive scale-up with short evaluation windows but conservative scale-down to avoid flapping. Example: evaluate 95th token latency every 15s, scale if >110ms for 20s, add 1 worker per event, cooldown 120s; scale down only after 10m of sustained low utilization. Prewarm: keep 1 burst worker warm during business hours and spin additional 1-2 from burst pool when queued length >20.
infra-bot: New presales case created: PS-4399.
nate: For cold starts: we should provide both warm-preforked workers and a fast warm path where model weights are memory-mapped to accelerate spin-up to ~10s for large models. Document that for the customer.
vijay: Security Qs: KMS details: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/GCP KMS; for Private deployments we can integrate on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11) — requires coordination with infra ops for key import. Also provide signed audit logs and per-request metadata export.
maria: Data residency: they asked for EU-only storage for logs. We can configure log sinks to a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket in-region. Note: request masking must be enabled for PII.
emma: Pricing draft: show two lines — Reserved plan (monthly GPU charge + usage-based burst token rate) and Simple blended plan (higher per-token but no commitment). Example numbers: reserved: $Xk/month per A30 equiv + $Y per 1M burst tokens; blended: $Z per 1M tokens. (Nate to fill actual numbers).
nate: I'll run cost calc and return a table. For the sales deck, convert to $/1M tokens for the mixed baseline+20% burst scenario.
aria: POC plan: 10-day sandbox + 3-day stress window. During stress window we'll run synthetic load at 2x expected peak for 20-minute bursts to validate autoscale and preheat. Provide load tool + scripts and a checklist for customer to open ports/SCIM metadata.
emma: Can someone paste a compact autoscale YAML we can hand to customer? Keep it simple.
arjun: Paste below (give them as example):
```
autoscale:
  measurement: token_95_latency_ms
  threshold_ms: 110
  eval_window_sec: 20
  scale_up: +1
  max_workers: 8
  scale_down_eval_sec: 600
  prewarm:
    keep_warm: 1
    warm_when_queue_gt: 20
  fallback_policy:
    route_to: quantized-int8
    trigger_queue_ms: 150
```
nate: Also add: prefer continuous batching=true, kv_cache_prefix=true, and set max_batch_size according to model (we'll recommend 64 for chat).
aria: Action items: nate -> cost numbers and $/1M tokens by EOD; vijay -> HSM/KMS sample wording and checklist; arjun -> autoscale snippet + explanation of warm paths; maria -> POC runbook and stress scripts. Emma will assemble and send to BlueFin.
emma: One more ask from customer: SSO + SCIM group sync. We support SAML + OIDC and SCIM provisioning. If they want group sync, we'll need their IdP metadata.
vijay: Note on SLA: reserved pool gives better latency guarantees; document fallback behavior so security/trust teams don't see silent failures (explicit fallbacks to quantized model and capacity tiering).
emate: typo (correction): nate: will deliver numbers tomorrow morning PST.
emma: Great, Ill follow up. :thumbsup:
